clue.text: Article Church Or State hosted by news presenter

parts.note: A is the indefinite article

indicators.note: a guest hosted by someone sits within their house, so the following pieces go inside the letters for news

parts.note: N is short for new, so news is two of them, NN
taken as written
MA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A newsreader introduces a debate article on Church versus State.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' looks like part of the definition, news presenter, but only 'presenter' defines; news is read as two Ns. MA is Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast anchor is the lead presenter who links a news programme together.

clue.text: An exceptional corpse is worth such veneration?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something exceptional is out of the ordinary, so the letters of the words that follow are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A remarkable dead body might deserve to be revered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptional' rearranges CORPSE IS WORTH after AN; the whole clue also hints at revering the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestor worship is the reverence of dead forebears, a kind of veneration paid to the departed.

clue.text: As beggar also supports church, a little drink's served up within

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece that supports another sits below it, so the word for also comes after
within signals that the small pieces sit inside the abbreviation for church
in a down clue, served up means the word for a little drink is written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Someone begging for church funds also gets a small tot of drink served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As beggar' defines a manner: humbly asking. In a down light, 'supports' puts the piece for also underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To come cap in hand is to ask humbly, like a beggar holding out a hat for coins.

clue.text: Some who do urinals use air freshener to stop it

definitions.text: use air freshener to stop it

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people who clean public toilets spray a freshener to prevent a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell, especially an unpleasant one, is what an air freshener is sprayed to mask.

clue.text: M&S skirts very big for supermodel

indicators.note: skirts as a verb means goes round the edge of, so the M and S surround the piece for very big

parts.note: the M and S of the store's name
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning very big

explanation.surface: Marks and Spencer skirts in big sizes for a famous catwalk model.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks and Spencer, a British high-street store; 'skirts' puts OS (outsize) between its M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Moss is a famous British fashion model, one of the original 1990s supermodels.

clue.text: Most of NHS nurses scrap seabird recipe, possibly Cumbrian

indicators.note: nurses in the sense of holding close, so the first piece takes another inside it
most of a word is all of it except the final letter, here dropping the closing S

parts.note: an ort is a scrap of leftover food
the erne is the sea eagle
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Health service nurses throw out a recipe for cooking a seabird, perhaps from the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims NHS to NH, which 'nurses' ORT; TERN is the tempting seabird, but ERNE is needed. Cumbria is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Cumbria, in the far north-west of England, is one example of a person from the north.

clue.text: Bless you, child, for approach in secret?

parts.note: ta is informal British thanks, as is bless you said in gratitude
a pup is a young animal, and a cheeky youngster

explanation.surface: A grateful parent thanks a child for creeping up quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you. To tap up is the British football term for illicitly approaching a player under contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapping up is making an underhand offer to someone contracted elsewhere, a covert approach.

clue.text: Set up trade in extremely attractive mosaic pieces

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from the bottom, so reversed

parts.note: taken as written
to sell is to trade goods

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Arranging a deal in very attractive mosaic tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SET into TES; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of attractive, A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessellae are the small square tiles fitted together to form a mosaic.

clue.text: Appropriate game — contact us for price, children

parts.note: POA, price on application, is what a seller prints instead of a price

explanation.surface: A notice about poaching game invites enquiries about prices for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' is a verb here, meaning to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Poaching is illegally taking game animals or fish, so stealing it for oneself.

clue.text: Old New Yorker finds Sunset Ave pretty violent

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters are thrown about wildly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A former resident finds a street in the city rather rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges SUNSET AVE PRETTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuyvesant was the last Dutch director-general of New Amsterdam, the colony that became New York.

clue.text: Great to get notes written by short people

parts.note: to cop is slang for to get or catch
IOUs are notes of debt written by people who are short of money

explanation.surface: Small people get a big pile of notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' means short of money, not small in height.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful, abundant in quantity, as in a great amount.

clue.text: Put new life into leisure facility

parts.note: rest is leisure time away from work
a facility is a skill or knack, as is art

explanation.surface: Renovate a leisure centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leisure facility' reads as a sports centre, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart something is to set it going again, reviving it.

clue.text: The odds of seeing weary guard

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the next word, first, third and fifth

parts.note: to try is to weary or tax, as in try someone's patience

explanation.surface: The chances of spotting a tired watchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The odds of' takes S, E and N from seeing; 'weary' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch at a gate or post.

clue.text: Shark upset short woman by river

indicators.note: short signals the last letter is cut off the word for upset

parts.note: threw means upset, as in threw someone off balance
she is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A shark has upset a small woman beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts the W from THREW; 'short woman' looks like one unit, but the shortening applies to upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The thresher is a large shark with a very long whip-like upper tail.

clue.text: Whacked a huge dog barking in middle of road

indicators.note: in middle of places the rearranged letters between the two letters for road

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

indicators.note: barking as in barking mad, so the letters go crazy and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A great hound is barking in the middle of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' rearranges A HUGE DOG, which goes 'in middle of' ST. Shagged out is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacked is informal for exhausted, and the answer is British slang for worn out.

clue.text: Granny appears in Oscars; the right idea — film's unrealistic

indicators.note: appears in means the word for granny is seen inside the letters for Oscars

parts.note: Oscar is O in the radio alphabet, so two of them give OO
nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
taken as written
a plan is an idea or scheme
ET is the Spielberg film about an alien

explanation.surface: A grandmother turns up at the Oscars, but the notion behind the film is far-fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscars' looks like the Academy Awards but stands for two Os, from the radio alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be off in another world is to be out of touch with reality, hopelessly unrealistic.

clue.text: Following type of circuit that is erratic, enter?

parts.note: an OR circuit is a logic gate in electronics
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: erratic means wandering irregularly, so the letters of the next word are moved about

explanation.surface: A runner on a course wanders erratically and asks whether to enter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following type' means a person who follows a course, though it reads like a description of a circuit; 'erratic' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An orienteer navigates a course with map and compass, finding and following control points.

clue.text: New note, one featured in some new coinage

indicators.note: featured in means the pieces appear within the rearranged letters
new signals the letters of the word before it are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a log is a written note or record
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A new note featuring one in some new coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'New' is an abbreviation, the second an anagram signal; 'featured in' sets the note and one inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression.

clue.text: Stupid cow needed my ring for this

definitions.text: Stupid cow needed my ring for this

indicators.note: stupid suggests muddled thinking, so the letters that follow are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude remark that a foolish woman needed a ring for her nuptials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' rearranges COW NEEDED MY RING; the whole clue also describes the event.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage service is where a ring is placed on the finger.

clue.text: Damsel somewhat distressed after betrayal of prince

definitions.text: Damsel somewhat distressed after betrayal of prince

parts.words: Damsel somewhat distressed after betrayal of prince
parts.note: read distressed as dis-tressed: the fairy-tale girl in the tower has her long hair cut off once her secret visits from a prince are revealed

explanation.surface: A damsel in distress after a prince betrays her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' puns on tresses: in the Grimm tale the witch shears off the heroine's hair after learning of the prince.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Grimm fairy tale, the tower-bound heroine loses her famous hair when the witch learns of the prince.

clue.text: Soft, thin piece of wood

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
lank means lean or thin

explanation.surface: A soft, thin length of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank is a long flat board of timber.

clue.text: Cut old wood fences

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so the word for wood surrounds the letter for old

parts.note: a grove is a small wood

explanation.surface: Chop down an old wood fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fences' is a verb meaning encloses, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel cut into a surface.

clue.text: Rock group INXS offered pointless rework of old single

parts.note: REM was an American rock band

indicators.note: pointless means without points of the compass, so the N and S are removed

explanation.surface: One rock band offers a remix of an old hit by another.
explanation.walkthrough: INXS is an Australian rock band; 'pointless' strips the compass points N and S, leaving IX.
explanation.definitionFit: A remix is a reworked version of an existing recording, such as an old single.

clue.text: Greek hero in top ratings, would you say?

parts.note: A as in A grade or class A, the top rating

indicators.note: would you say asks the solver to hear the word for ratings spoken

parts.note: ratings are ordinary sailors, also called jacks or jack tars

explanation.surface: A Greek hero appears in the top ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ratings' looks like a league table but means sailors; JACKS sounds like JAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a mighty Greek warrior at the siege of Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Earth filling must stop?

indicators.note: filling means the letter for Earth goes inside the phrase for must

parts.note: have to means must

explanation.surface: Earth used as filling has to be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: Heave to is a sailing term for bringing a ship to a stop; the question mark flags the nautical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave to is to bring a sailing vessel to a halt by setting the sails against each other.

clue.text: Informal play areas flank both sides of idyllic island

parts.note: a jam is an informal music session where players improvise

indicators.note: flank means stand on either side of, so the outer pieces enclose the inner

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so areas give two

indicators.note: both sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Casual playgrounds surround an idyllic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both sides of' takes I and C from idyllic, which sit between JAMA and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica is a Caribbean island nation south of Cuba.

clue.text: Good parts for a stud?

indicators.note: parts as a verb means separates, so the word for good splits the phrase for a

parts.note: per means for a or for each, as in two pounds per person
OK is informal for good or acceptable

explanation.surface: Good attributes for a breeding stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: PER means for a, as in two per person; 'parts' is a verb. Stud is a variety of the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud is a form of the card game in which some cards are dealt face up.

clue.text: Duty-free rubbish bags by former European politician

indicators.note: bags means holds in a bag, so the word for rubbish wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish
X is the times sign, as in three by four
ex means former
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Junk bagged up by an ex-MEP is free of duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' is a verb meaning encloses; 'by' supplies X, the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt from tax means no levy is charged, as with duty-free goods.
